message.content:
Below are two ways you can create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Note**  
> *Google Cloud does not use the “EC2” terminology – that’s Amazon Web Services. In GCP the service is called **Compute Engine**.*

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Replace <PROJECT_ID> and <ZONE> with your own values
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=<PROJECT_ID> \
  --zone=<ZONE> \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1` requests one RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | Sets a 100 GB SSD boot disk. Adjust as needed. |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keeps the instance running during maintenance events. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (adjust scopes if you need tighter security). |
| `--tags` | Allows HTTP/HTTPS traffic if you plan to expose services. |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, just change the `--machine-type` and `--accelerator` values accordingly.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly, here’s a minimal `curl` example. Make sure you have a valid OAuth 2.0 access token (`<ACCESS_TOKEN>`).

```bash
PROJECT_ID="<PROJECT_ID>"
ZONE="<ZONE>"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
EOF

curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### Explanation of the JSON payload

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name. |
| `machineType` | Full resource path to the machine type. |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk configuration (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image, 100 GB SSD). |
| `accelerators[0]` | One RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Uses the default VPC network and assigns an external IP. |
| `serviceAccounts[0]` | Default service account with full Cloud Platform scope. |
| `tags.items` | Network tags for firewall rules (HTTP/HTTPS). |

> **Authentication** – Replace `<ACCESS_TOKEN>` with a bearer token obtained via OAuth 2.0 (e.g., using `gcloud auth print-access-token`).  

---

## Quick Checklist

- [ ] **Project ID** – Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` with your GCP project ID.
- [ ] **Zone** – Choose a zone that supports the RTX A6000 (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`).
- [ ] **GPU quota** – Ensure you have a GPU quota for the RTX A6000 in the selected zone.
- [ ] **Billing** – Verify that billing is enabled for the project.
- [ ] **Firewall** – If you need inbound traffic, add firewall rules for the tags `http-server` and `https-server`.

Once the instance is created, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=$ZONE
```

Enjoy your new GPU‑powered Ubuntu 20.04 instance!
